planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated starts after all frost danger has passed in a container or hanging basket with well-drained, fertile potting mix.

directions: Part of the Superbells Magic line, this double-flowered calibrachoa opens a soft yellow and gradually shifts toward pink as individual blooms age, so a single plant carries both colors at once for a two-tone effect. Its mounding, trailing habit cascades over container edges and needs no deadheading to keep flowering from spring through hard frost. Grow in full to part sun with regular feeding, since the heavy, continuous bloom is nutrient-demanding; trim back if stems become leggy by midsummer to refresh growth.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated starts after last frost in well-drained, fertile potting mix in a container or hanging basket.

directions: Superbells Cardinal Star produces vivid red, petunia-like flowers marked with a sharp yellow star radiating from the throat, giving a bold two-color punch on a mounding, trailing plant. Flowers appear in overwhelming numbers continuously from spring through frost without deadheading. Grow in full to part sun in moist, well-drained, fertile soil, feeding regularly since the nonstop bloom draws heavily on nutrients; its cascading stems suit hanging baskets, window boxes, and container edges.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated starts after last frost in well-drained potting mix; calibrachoa resents constantly wet soil, so containers with good drainage perform best.

directions: Superbells Coral Sun carries bright coral-orange petals that brighten toward a sunny yellow eye at the center, giving a warm, glowing bicolor effect on a compact mounding-trailing plant. It blooms nonstop from spring through fall without deadheading. Grow in full to part sun in well-drained potting mix, since calibrachoa performs poorly in soils that stay saturated; feed regularly to sustain the heavy continuous flower display in containers and hanging baskets.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated starts after last frost in well-drained, fertile potting mix in a container or hanging basket.

directions: This fully double calibrachoa opens in an intense magenta with a deeper magenta-red blush concentrated toward the flower center, adding richness that single-flowered Superbells lack. Its mounding, trailing stems spill over container edges and bloom continuously from planting to hard frost without deadheading. Grow in full to part sun in moist, well-drained soil with good drainage, feeding regularly to keep the dense double blooms coming all season in hanging baskets and window boxes.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after last frost in rich, well-drained soil or potting mix; this vigorous selection also performs well planted directly in landscape beds.

directions: Supertunia Pink Tiara bears princess-pink flowers with a luminous white throat that seems to glow from the center of each bloom, set on an unusually vigorous, spreading plant. It flowers continuously from spring to fall without deadheading. Grow in full to part sun with consistent moisture, since petunias decline if allowed to wilt severely between waterings; its low, wide habit suits front-of-border landscape plantings as well as large hanging baskets and mixed containers.

scientific_name: Petunia x hybrida 'Supertunia Picasso in Purple'

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after last frost in rich, well-drained soil or potting mix.

directions: Supertunia Picasso in Purple carries bicolor blooms of rich purple edged in a painterly rim of mint green, giving each flower a hand-brushed, artistic look. The mounding-to-trailing plant can spill up to three feet and blooms nonstop from planting to hard frost without deadheading. Grow in full to part sun with even moisture, feeding regularly; it works equally well edging the front of a landscape bed or filling and spilling from mixed containers and hanging baskets.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after last frost in rich, well-drained soil or potting mix; elevated hanging baskets let its long trailing stems drape freely.

directions: Supertunia Silver produces clean white flowers on a very low, wide-spreading plant whose trailing stems can reach up to three feet, making it one of the longest-trailing Supertunia selections. It blooms continuously from planting to hard frost without deadheading and tolerates heat and short dry spells once established. Grow in full to part sun with even moisture and regular feeding; trim back by a third in midsummer if growth becomes thin or leggy to encourage a fresh flush.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after last frost in well-drained soil or potting mix; this mounded selection is bred for landscape beds as well as containers.

directions: Part of the Blanket series, a petunia line bred for weather-tough, mounded garden-bed performance rather than long trailing, this selection carries fragrant pink flowers over a dense, rounded habit from spring to hard frost. Deadhead as needed to keep flowering strong through the season. Grow in full to part sun with average, consistent moisture; its compact mound suits mixed landscape beds and container fillers alike, and it draws butterflies and hummingbirds to the garden.
